body:
Part of #87. Complexity: medium. Size: M.

The entry point imports sync, hosting, viewer and parsing code before command dispatch. Packaged --version took 76 ms and 66 MiB; a version-only prototype took 39 ms and 50 MiB. Intermediate dist startup differed from the packaged bundle.

Scope:

- Add a lightweight help/version dispatch and defer expensive command implementation loading.
- Preserve the private deletion-worker and service-owner preflight entry paths, exit codes, command parsing and public output.
- Measure the final ncc/npm artifact; source-level lazy imports alone do not prove reduced bundle startup.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Installed --help/--version avoid executing unrelated subsystems and retain exact behavior.
- [ ] Ordinary commands, internal child entry points and detached viewer/worker startup continue to work.
- [ ] Benchmark direct installed CLI startup separately from npm/npx launcher overhead on both runtime lines.

No implementation dependency; benchmark and release-policy coordination remain part of #87.

Release routing: implement compatibility-preserving work on 0.7.x for Node 20 and forward-port to 1.x. If preserving current contracts is not possible, move that portion to 1.x rather than changing the compatibility line.

Source references at the exploration baseline:

- [packages/cli/src/index.ts](https://github.com/deveshsangwan/html-inbox/blob/1ae641ac088e5e504fc222e39726ad631b342b8c/packages/cli/src/index.ts)
- [packages/cli/package.json](https://github.com/deveshsangwan/html-inbox/blob/1ae641ac088e5e504fc222e39726ad631b342b8c/packages/cli/package.json)
- [scripts/package-smoke.mjs](https://github.com/deveshsangwan/html-inbox/blob/1ae641ac088e5e504fc222e39726ad631b342b8c/scripts/package-smoke.mjs)

Measurements, where cited, come from the 7 November 2026 isolated Linux/Node 24.19 study with warm filesystem caches. Recheck current code and reproduce relevant behavior before implementation; prototype gains are not production guarantees.

Execution and acceptance gates added at the maintainer's request:

- One dedicated T3 issue-owner thread and at least one focused PR. Dependent changes may use a PR stack; identify the immediate parent and release line.
- Development uses GPT-6.1 Sol High or Extra High. Two fresh independent reviewers inspect the same pinned commit: a Sol functionality review and a Claude Code Sonnet 5.5 Medium code-quality review. Both receive the full issue, diff and measurement evidence. Resolve or explicitly record every finding.
- Every optimization implementation must demonstrate a repeatable improvement in elapsed time, CPU, memory, I/O, disk use or responsiveness, beyond observed measurement noise. Preselect the affected operations and success metric. Record baseline/candidate commits, environment, commands, sample counts, raw results and spread, absolute/relative changes and regressions. Compare equivalent workloads and behavior. Run benchmarks without competing measurement jobs.
- Preserve the applicable correctness, security, validation, durability and compatibility contracts. Runtime upgrades, cache warmth or relaxed guarantees must not be mistaken for a code optimization.
- If no practical benefit is demonstrated, reject the production change and use the PR to record the experiment and decision. Investigation PRs need a justified go/no-go result. Policy and benchmark prerequisites must identify the measured work they enable and must not claim a runtime speedup.
- Keep the PR draft until the issue-specific behavior, measurement and both review gates pass. Merging and releasing are separate actions.

Dedicated T3 thread: <t3-thread://v2/b48ea996-697f-47b9-b203-e68d42cd46b8/mcp:launch:ab86db7b77bf196958dc36da28bfc42ead112707f68be565944f43b251b8e9ff>
title: Load only the command modules needed for CLI startup
